important.name: Draft-before-lease split can silently clobber a queued update drained in between
important.summary:
The split now reads the item (step 1) and drafts its overrides (step 2) before it takes the lease (step 3). Step 4 claims the dry run catches whatever changed meanwhile, but it only refuses a split or retired id. The same PR adds `inbox put --update`, so a drain (todo-watch, or another session's `todo-edit --update`) can land new `files`, `summary`, `severity` or `loe` on that item in the gap; the split spec then overrides those fields with values drafted from the old copy, and the dry run passes. The update disappears with no problem line and no `overwrote` notice. Under the old lease-first order this window did not exist. Concurrency giveth, concurrency taketh away.

Also (docs): Split step 3 (todo-editor.md:136-139) tells the agent to rerun `TS lease acquire --wait 300` up to 3 times in all when the `problem:` line names a holder (decision D1A). The Stop conditions (todo-editor.md:288-290) say: report and stop, do not improvise, when a script exits 2, with the only listed exception being one spec fix for split, sync, add or update. A held-lease refusal exits 2 and is not a spec fix, so a literal reading stops on the first refusal. That drops the 3-try budget the plan settled on, and the general rule can override the step-specific one.
fix: In todo-editor.md split step 3 or 4: after the lease is taken, re-read the item and compare it with the step 1 read; when a field the spec overrides (or inherits into a part) changed, redraft those fields before the dry run.
Have `split --dry-run` take an item digest from the draft (for example `--expect-digest`) and refuse when the live item no longer matches, so the driver catches the drift instead of agent prose.

In todo-editor.md:288-289, extend the exception: `(relay the problem: line verbatim, after one spec fix for split, sync, add or update, or after the third held-lease refusal of a split's lease acquire)`.
Or add a sentence after todo-editor.md:290: `A split's lease acquire refused for a held lease is rerun as split step 3 says; only the third refusal stops the run.`

minor.name: Update step 1 pushes a summary rewrite the guidance may not touch
minor.summary:
Update step 1 (todo-editor.md:243-245) tells the agent to check the guidance's claims 'as add level 1 does: cite `path:line` in `summary`'. Step 2 (todo-editor.md:246-249) says to set only the fields the guidance touches, and each value replaces the field whole. Guidance such as `severity 4: the parser drops rows` touches `severity` and `why_ranked`. Step 1 still sends the agent to write a citation into `summary`, and a `summary` update replaces the item's existing summary text whole, which can drop content the guidance never asked to change.

Also (overall): todo-editor.md update step 1 says to check the guidance's claims 'as add level 1 does: cite `path:line` in `summary`', but step 2 limits new values to the fields the guidance touches. For guidance that only changes `severity` (the skill's own example, `-- severity 4: the parser drops rows`), the two steps conflict: either the agent rewrites `summary` the guidance did not touch, or it skips the citation step 1 requires.

Also (system_shape): todo-editor.md update step 2 (lines 246-254) lets an update set `needs_decision`, `decision_question` and `status`, says each value replaces the field whole, and points to the sync step 3 shapes and schema checks. An update has no way to delete a field, though, and the catalog schema (TodoCatalog.schema.json, needs_decision else-branch around line 962-967) requires `decision_question` to be null when `needs_decision` is false. Status `NEEDS_DECISION` also requires `needs_decision` true. So resolving a decision, a natural update, takes three coordinated fields in one update: `needs_decision: false`, `decision_question: null` and a status other than NEEDS_DECISION. Sync step 3 never mentions null (it lists `decision_question` among the string fields), so an agent setting only `needs_decision: false` gets a `problem:` line and may burn its single spec fix.
fix: Reword todo-editor.md:244-245 to: `check its claims as **add** level 1 does; when the update sets `summary`, cite `path:line` there, carry over the existing text that still holds, and write a claim the tree neither confirms nor refutes as `unverified`.`
Scope the citation: 'cite `path:line` in `summary` when the update sets `summary` (else in `why_ranked`)', or say verified claims go into whichever text field the update sets.
Add to todo-editor.md update step 2: 'To close a decision, set `needs_decision` false, `decision_question` null and a `status` other than `NEEDS_DECISION` in the same update.'

minor.name: `put_updates` docstring promises TodoSyncError for a failed inbox write
minor.summary: The Raises section says `TodoSyncError: ... or a failed inbox write`, but `_write_items` cleans up and re-raises whatever failed, which is the raw `OSError` from `write_atomic` or `_replace_with_retry`. `put_updates` does not wrap it (unlike `put`, which wraps only when issues were filed). The driver catches `OSError` too, so behavior is fine; the contract text is wrong.
fix: Reword the Raises section: `TodoSyncError: an unreadable spec or an update the catalog refuses (nothing is written). OSError: a failed inbox write (every file of the put still present is deleted).`

minor.name: A malformed update file is refused with an add-spec reason
minor.summary: `_holds_updates` routes a file to the update path only when `updates` is a list. A queued file holding `{"updates": {...}}` or `{"updates": null}` (a hand-edited or truncated file) goes to `add_items` instead. Its `.reason.txt` then reads `add spec ...: expected an object with a 'items' list`, which sends the person to the wrong format.
fix: Route on the key alone: `return isinstance(doc, dict) and "updates" in doc`. `read_spec(path, "updates")` then refuses the file with an `update spec ...: expected an object with a 'updates' list` reason.

minor.name: _resolve docstring promises a doubled id raises; resolve_ids dedupes it
minor.summary: The `_resolve` docstring says "a retired, split, unknown or doubled id raises". `todo_ids.resolve_ids` drops repeats (`if text not in by_kind[kind]`), so an update whose id reads `k7qf, todo-K7QF` resolves to one id and is accepted. Only two different ids reach the `names N ids` refusal. Accepting the repeat is harmless, but the docstring states a refusal the code never makes.
fix: Reword the docstring to "a retired, split or unknown id, or a raw naming more than one id, raises".
Or, if a repeated id should be refused, check `len(todo_ids._pieces([raw])) != 1` before resolving and raise the same `update n names ...` message.

minor.name: todo_sync.md intro and add section still describe the inbox as items only
minor.summary:
The todo_sync.py module docstring (todo_sync.py:3) now says the script queues 'items and field updates in the inbox'. todo_sync.md:5-6 still says it 'queues drafted items in an inbox', and the `add` section intro (todo_sync.md:162) says 'Adds items to the catalog, either from a spec file or from the inbox'. In the `--inbox` row (todo_sync.md:168), 'When any item lands, the page is rendered and the check run' can be read as excluding a drain where only updates landed. The drain does render and check then: inbox.py `_finish(cfg, day, bool(got.accepted), ...)` counts accepted update files.

Also (overall): An update-only drain also renders and checks (`_finish(..., bool(got.accepted), ...)`), but the todo_sync.md `--inbox` row says 'When any item lands, the page is rendered and the check run', and the `_finish` docstring says 'Run the follow-up when items landed'. Both read as if a drain that only applied updates skips the render and check.

Also (roast): The `--inbox` row of the `add` table now describes queued updates, but it keeps 'When any item lands, the page is rendered and the check run'. A drain where only updates land also writes, renders and checks (the docstrings and drain() say 'when anything landed').
fix: todo_sync.md:5-6: `queues drafted items and field updates in an inbox`; todo_sync.md:162: `Adds items to the catalog, either from a spec file or from the inbox (which also applies queued field updates)`; todo_sync.md:168: `When anything lands (an item or an update), the page is rendered and the check run.`
todo_sync.md line 168: 'When anything lands (an item or an update), the page is rendered and the check run.' inbox.py `_finish` docstring: 'when anything landed'.
In todo_sync.md line 168, change 'When any item lands' to 'When anything lands (an added item or an update)'.

minor.name: todo_sync.py Locking docstring still states a flat 10-second wait
minor.summary: The PR updated the Locking paragraph of todo_sync.md (line 57-58) to say `lease acquire --wait SECONDS` waits that long instead of 10 seconds, but the matching paragraph of the driver's own module docstring (todo_sync.py:125-129, 'A lock another owner holds is waited on for 10 seconds, then refused naming its owner, mode and age') was left unchanged. The two descriptions of the same locking rule now disagree; the `lease acquire` entry higher in the same docstring (lines 94-99) already names --wait, so the docstring also contradicts itself.
fix: In plugins/harness/scripts/todo_sync.py:127-128 change 'is waited on for 10 seconds, then refused' to 'is waited on for 10 seconds (``lease acquire --wait SECONDS`` waits that long instead), then refused', mirroring todo_sync.md.

minor.name: --wait accepts inf, so lease acquire can wait without a bound
minor.summary:
`_seconds` turns `inf` or `1e999` into `float('inf')`, which passes `value >= 0`. `catalog_lock._acquire` then sets `deadline = monotonic() + inf`, so `remaining` never reaches 0. `lease acquire` blocks until the holder releases or goes stale (a lease only after 30 minutes), whatever Bash timeout the caller set. The help text promises a number of seconds before the refusal.

Also (overall): `_seconds` rejects negatives and NaN (`not value >= 0`), but `float('inf')` passes, so `lease acquire --wait inf` sets a deadline of `monotonic() + inf`. It then waits until the held lease turns stale (30 minutes) or forever on a held write lock. That is far past the 600 s Bash cap the 300 s value was chosen to fit, and the help text says the value is a number of seconds.

Also (roast): `_seconds` rejects NaN and negative values, but `float('inf')` passes `value >= 0`. `catalog_lock._acquire` then gets an infinite deadline, and `lease acquire` blocks until the holder lets go, however long that takes. The help promises a number of seconds and the agent budget assumes a bounded wait.
fix: In `_seconds`, `import math` and refuse non-finite values: `if not (math.isfinite(value) and value >= 0): raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(...)`.

In `_seconds`, also refuse a non-finite value: `if not (math.isfinite(value) and value >= 0): raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(...)`, and add `inf` to the parametrized cases in tests/scripts/test_todo_sync_lease_wait.py::test_the_wait_is_a_non_negative_number.

In `_seconds`, refuse a non-finite value: `if not math.isfinite(value) or value < 0: raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(...)`, and add `"inf"` to the parametrized cases of `test_the_wait_is_a_non_negative_number`.

minor.name: Sibling drain readers miss the new update parts of the inbox line
minor.summary: `add --inbox` now also applies queued field updates, and todo_sync.md says any agent may queue them, so a `/harness:sync-gh-todo` or `/harness:add-todo` drain can land updates queued by another run. Those skills still read only the old shapes: sync-gh-todo pins the failure text as `problem: inbox: added <ids>, then: <reason>` and sends every other `problem:` line to 'the queued items stay in the inbox'. When only updates landed (the skill's own items refused), inbox.py `_landed_text` produces `problem: inbox: updated <ids>, then: ...`, which those skills misreport as nothing landed. The success line can also carry `updated M item(s)` and `overwrote` parts the prose does not describe. The plan's sweep S1 kept both skills unchanged.
fix: In sync-gh-todo SKILL.md Step 4 (lines 73-82) and add-todo SKILL.md Step 4 (lines 80-88), add that the line may carry `updated M item(s): ...` and `overwrote <id> <field>` parts for updates other runs queued, and that a `problem:` line opening `inbox: added` or `inbox: updated` means those changes landed and only the follow-up failed, matching todo-edit SKILL.md Step 3.

minor.name: Shared guidance across per-id update agents has no routing rule
minor.summary:
Step 2 sends every `--split`/`--update` agent 'the same guidance'. The agent's update section (todo-editor.md:241-248) reads Guidance as what to change for its one id and sets 'the ones the guidance touches'. For `--update todo-a, todo-b -- todo-a severity 4; todo-b loe M`, both agents see both instructions, and nothing in either file says to apply only the part that names the agent's own id. Either agent can then queue the other id's change on its own item, and the drain applies it.

Also (skill_package): Step 4 says 'Relay every agent's reply as it stands, one per id', but Step 2 has `--retire` and `--refresh` make one Agent call for all their ids (refresh has none). Only split and update produce one reply per id. Step 2 also says refresh makes one call 'for all their ids', although Step 1 forbids ids on `--refresh`.

Also (roast): Step 1 passes ids as typed and leaves canonicalization to the script. That was safe when one agent got the whole list, but `--split` and `--update` now dispatch one agent per id. `--split k7qf, todo-K7QF` starts two opus agents on one item: the second waits on the lease (up to 3 x 300 s) only to hit a 'was split into' problem line. `--update k7qf, todo-k7qf` queues two updates, and the later one overwrites the first.

Also (roast): Each split agent waits at most 3 x `--wait 300` for the lease, and each holder keeps it through the dry run, the real run and **finish** (check, prose fixes, release). With N ids dispatched at once, the last split waits for N-1 full applies; past roughly 15 minutes it ends on its third refusal and its drafted spec is never applied. Neither the skill nor the agent caps N or says what happens to the leftovers.
fix: Add a sentence to SKILL.md Step 2 (or to todo-editor.md update step 2): when the guidance names several ids, each agent applies only what it says about its own id, plus what applies to all.
Have Step 2 split guidance written per id (`id: text`) and send each agent only its own part.

SKILL.md:84: 'Relay every agent's reply as it stands (one per id for split and update), then the Step 3 line for an update.' SKILL.md:46: '`--retire` makes one `Agent` call for all its ids, and `--refresh` one call.'
In SKILL.md Step 2, before dispatching per id, drop an id whose canonical form (lowercased, `todo-` prefix added) repeats an earlier one, and name the dropped duplicates in the Step 4 report.

In SKILL.md Step 2, cap `--split` at a small number of ids per message (for example 4) and dispatch the rest in a later message, or say in Step 4 that a split ending on a held-lease refusal left its spec at `<state_dir>/todo-sync/split-<id>.json` for a rerun.

minor.name: Step 3 drain-line description misstates the opening and the problem form
minor.summary:
Step 3 says the drain 'prints one line: `inbox: updated M item(s): ...`' with an `added N item(s)` part when other items landed, but `drain_lines` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/inbox.py:443-452) puts the `added` part first, so a mixed drain opens `inbox: added ...; updated ...`. The partial-failure case is described as a `problem:` line that 'opens with `inbox: updated` or `inbox: added`', yet the line the script prints opens `problem: inbox: ...` (inbox.py:411). A literal read compares `problem: inbox: updated ...` with `inbox: updated`, finds no match, falls to 'Otherwise the queued updates stay in the inbox' and reports landed updates as not applied. sync-gh-todo spells the form out (`problem: inbox: added <ids>, then: <reason>`); add-todo shares the ambiguous wording.

Also (system_shape): SKILL.md Step 1 (lines 28-33) passes ids as typed and leaves canonicalization to the script, which was fine when one agent got every id. Step 2 (lines 45-49) now dispatches one agent per id for --split and --update, so `--update k7qf, todo-k7qf` (or `--split` with a repeated id) starts two agents on one item. For splits, the second agent waits up to 300 s for the lease only to fail its dry run. For updates, the todo-watch mod drains after each completed todo-editor agent (plugins/todo-watch/README.md:107-108), so the two agents' queued updates can land in separate drains. The later one then silently replaces fields the earlier one set: `_absorb_updates` (inbox.py) tracks `seen` only within a single drain. Step 3 (lines 70-72) still promises 'an `overwrote <id> <field>` part when two queued updates set the same field'.

(`todo_sync.py inbox put`)', and its intro (line 10) says the drain 'adds' items. minor.name: Kind refusal case matches any update-1 error
